Subject: Approval request: HelioMed Dedicated GPU variance & temporary reservation hold

Team —

HelioMed (trialing a near-term clinical imaging app) has asked for two non-standard asks to close a Dedicated deal that would convert to a 12-month reserved commitment after the POC:

1) Temporary reservation hold (30 days): they want us to pause their 4x A100 reservation billing for the first 30 days while they validate H100 performance in our environment. During the hold they request the ability to burst onto H100s (up to +50% peak) with a capped overage rate.

2) GPU family variance: they want H100s guaranteed for burst windows and the option to substitute A100->H100 permanently if benchmarks hit their SLA. They are requesting a 25% discount on base hourly reservation rate for year-1 if we accept the temporary hold and the burst-cap agreement.

Why this matters: HelioMed is a mid-market imaging SaaS with strong reference potential in healthcare. Their POC spend (hosted + Dedicated) projects to $780k ARR post-conversion. They are requesting this structure because their clinical benchmarks are sensitive to fp16 perf on H100s; they don't want to pay full reservation while validating.

Requested approvals (exec decision items):
- Approve a 30-day reservation billing hold (no invoice for reserved units during that window), with a contractual amendment capturing start/end dates and acceptance criteria.
- Allow up to +50% burst capacity on H100s during the hold; cap overage at $3.25/hour per H100-equivalent (we would credit toward reservation if they convert).
- Approve a one-time Year-1 discount of 25% on the reservation rate if HelioMed converts within 45 days of the hold ending.

Attached: HelioMed proposal v3 (pricing scenarios) and Redwood pricing scenarios workbook with margin models.

Ask: Vivek/Aditya/Marcus/Laura — can we get a fast-path decision by EOD Friday? HelioMed needs commercial language for procurement.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
